overview: The OV7670 is a genuinely low-level camera module: it doesn't compress images or offer a simple 'give me a JPEG' interface — it streams raw pixel data continuously over an 8-bit parallel bus alongside clock and sync signals, meaning the receiving microcontroller has to actively capture pixels in real time as they arrive. That makes it a poor match for a plain Arduino Uno (not enough pins or speed) and a natural fit for boards with more I/O and processing headroom, like an STM32 or an FPGA. Camera settings (resolution, color format, exposure) are configured separately over SCCB, a two-wire protocol nearly identical to I2C.
simpleSummary: A basic camera chip that streams raw pixel data directly, needing the microcontroller to capture it live.

specifications.outputFormat: Raw parallel data — RGB565, YUV, or raw Bayer, no onboard JPEG compression
specifications.dataInterface: 8-bit parallel data bus + PCLK/VSYNC/HREF timing signals

pinMap.name: SIOC
pinMap.function: SCCB clock line (configuration interface, similar to I2C SCL).

pinMap.name: SIOD
pinMap.function: SCCB data line (configuration interface, similar to I2C SDA).

pinMap.name: VSYNC
pinMap.function: Frame sync — marks the start of a new video frame.

pinMap.name: HREF
pinMap.function: Line/row sync — marks valid pixel data within a row.

pinMap.name: PCLK
pinMap.function: Pixel clock — one pulse per pixel byte transferred on the data bus.
pinMap.gotcha: Capturing this data reliably requires either DMA or a very tight interrupt loop — a plain Arduino Uno cannot keep up with the pixel clock rate at full resolution.

pinMap.name: PWDN
pinMap.function: Power-down control — HIGH puts the sensor into low-power standby.

useCases.title: FPGA-based image processing
useCases.scenario: Common teaching example for capturing and processing raw video frames in FPGA coursework.

useCases.title: STM32-based low-level vision project
useCases.scenario: Capture frames via DMA on an STM32's camera interface peripheral for simple onboard image processing.

oftenConfusedWith: ESP32-CAM (handles the capture complexity onboard, exposes a simple higher-level API)
oftenUpgradedTo: ESP32-CAM or Raspberry Pi Camera Module for a much simpler capture pipeline
